paragraphs: Rabbi Chanan son of Pitum, a tanna, is mentioned in [Taanit 22b](https://www.sefaria.org/Taanit.22b.13). Hyman also refers to Levi bar Pitum in Yuchasin and directs the reader to his entry.[^1][^2][^3]

notes.text: The supplied heading reads Pitus, while the notice gives Pitum. [Heilprin](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=2948&lang=en) has the Pitum headword.
The linked Taanit calls Chanan ben Pitum a student of Rabbi Akiva and has him report the ruling in Rabbi Akiva’s name.

Hyman’s printed notice (vol. III, p. 1010) is headed פיטום, Pitum, where the supplied text has פיטוס, Pitus. The consulted Taanit 22b names Rabbi Chanan ben Pitum, a student who reports in Rabbi Akiva’s name. The reference to Levi bar Pitum in Yuchasin is Hyman’s report, and the exact Yuchasin passage remains unverified.
